labels.label: thm:upper
labels.notes: Read against perforated.tex l.860-895 (the definitions at l.862-869, the statement at l.871-879, the proof at l.881-895). Hypotheses on psi: the paper takes the minimiser of ||grad psi||^2 subject to psi = 1 on dSigma and int psi = 0. thm_upper takes EVERY psi in D with IsCapDCompetitor (tr psi = 1 bvol_j-a.e. on every B_j, Bochner int of val psi against vol_g = 0) and MemLp (val psi) L^{p*}. The paper's minimiser is one of these, so the paper's statement is an instance. The MemLp guard adds nothing: with an honest norm, the paper's own proviso rho < 1 already forces ||psi||_{p*} < oo (rho = oo otherwise), and W^{1,2} is contained in L^{p*} in the setting. In Lean, without the guard, an infinite norm would give the junk rho = 0. Conclusion: thetaDOf psi / (1 + thetaDOf psi) * Fq 1 / (1 - rhoOf psi)^2. This parses as ((theta_D/(1+theta_D)) F_g(1))/(1-rho)^2, the printed right-hand side, with theta_D = a_N ||grad psi||^2/(c_N S) (l.866) and rho = ||psi||_{L^{p*}}/V^{1/p*} (l.873, eLpNorm toReal over (vol univ).toReal^(1/p*)). lambda_d is infF g (fun _ => c_N), i.e. inf F_g, the model of record's lambda (DEC-186). The proviso rho < 1 is carried as hρ. The remaining hypotheses are hN : 3 <= N and finite vol/bvol (compactness). thm_upper does not need vol != 0 or a non-null B_j (it splits cases), and the docstring checklist says so truthfully. The instance-implicit finite measures are the strict library's reading of compactness. The infimum form thm_upper_capD (cap_D a real inf over competitors with L^{p*} values, cap_D != top) covers the paper's cap_D with no minimiser needed. The l.866-869 comparisons cap* <= cap_D and theta <= theta_D (capStar_le_capD, theta_le_thetaDOf/theta_le_thetaD) carry S != 0, which follows from the standing n >= 1 of DEC-186, and ell(psi) = -1 is proved as printed. Junk: dirichlet = 0 at infinite energy could put Lean's inf F below the paper's lambda, which would weaken any upper bound. The SCOPE discloses this, and upperTest_sStar closes it: u_{s*} is an explicit competitor of energy s*^2 ||grad psi||^2, finite for the paper's psi, with an honest trace (the constant 1 - s*) and honest L^{p*} norm, attaining the bound. Satisfiability: thm_upper_strong is witnessed on the toy model (toy_thm_upper_strong). thm_upper's rho < 1 is the paper's own proviso and is satisfiable, for instance on the Euclidean 3-ball (rho = 0.874, see lossy_check). The mark is correct. The REPORT finding that the minimiser's existence is not proved in the paper is true (no proof at l.862-869 or elsewhere). It is the standard direct-method fact, though (psi - 1 in W^{1,2}_0, coercivity by Friedrichs, strict convexity on a closed affine constraint), so it is a routine omission rather than an error.

labels.label: rem:notF1
labels.notes: Read against perforated.tex l.359-371. Every assertion is proved in rem_notF1: (i) F_g(1) = c_N S/V^{(N-2)/N}. (ii) For phi with int phi = 0 (values in L^{p*}, traces in L^{p#}: consequences of phi in W^{1,2} in the setting), the gradient term is exactly eps^2 ||grad phi||^2, d/d eps|_0 F_g(1 + eps phi) exists and equals firstVariation phi, which is term for term the printed 2c_N/V^{(N-2)/N} sum_j |B_j|^{-1/(N-1)} int_{B_j} phi (I rederived the formula: the denominator's derivative vanishes because int phi = 0, and 2/p# - 1 = -1/(N-1)), and it is < 0 when phi <= 0 and not == 0 on dSigma. (iii) Such phi exist. (iv) There is a competitor u with F_g(u) < F_g(1), and inf F_g < F_g(1). (v) kappa < 1. vol != 0 and a non-null B_j are standing (DEC-186, n >= 1), and the remark is false without them (F_g(1) = 0). RULING on the carried competitor psi (the closer's question): MARKED, not partial. Reasons. (1) On the abstract model some richness hypothesis on D is necessary: with D = R (val c = tr c = the constant c, d = 0, one = 1) every competitor is c*1, F_g(c*1) = F_g(1) by homogeneity, so inf F_g = F_g(1) and the remark fails. Any abstract-layer statement of rem:notF1 must therefore carry something that reads 'D is W^{1,2}(Sigma)'. (2) The carried hypothesis is a fact of the paper's own setting, not an added restriction. In W^{1,2}(Sigma) of a compact manifold with non-empty boundary such a psi exists: the paper names it at l.862 ('the classical equilibrium potential'), its l.367 quantifies over such phi as existing, and the companion's proof (Yamabegap.tex l.741) says 'Such phi exist (take phi = -1 near dSigma ...)'. So it is not a reading the paper leaves open (kb 0006). (3) Precedent: the strict, marked rem:sign (Yamabe/Quotient.lean infF_lt_Fq_one, kappa_lt_one, rem_sign) carries a bounded cutoff chi with tr chi = 1, int chi < V, and its SCOPE names 'a smooth collar cutoff chi' as part of the formalization of record under DEC-186. The psi hypothesis is implied by chi (exists_isCapDCompetitor_of_cutoff, using only chi's value bound and measurability, not its trace bound), so rem_notF1 assumes no more than the marked rem:sign. rem_notF1_of_cutoff gives (iv)-(v) directly under (a subset of) rem:sign's hypotheses, and composing exists_isCapDCompetitor_of_cutoff with rem_notF1 gives the full assembly. (4) It is satisfiable: toy_rem_notF1 discharges every hypothesis on the two-point model. The same junk exposure as rem:sign applies (an infinite-energy psi makes (iv) junk-true), and it is covered by the same strict-SCOPE obligation on the Riemannian instance. One wording gap: the SCOPE bullet calls (iii) proved 'in full' without saying that it rests on the carried psi (see the findings).

lossy_check: My own argument, confirming the REPORT's finding. If psi is a competitor in L^{p*} (hence in L^1, V < oo), then for every real s, int_Sigma u_s = int 1 - s int psi = V. Hoelder against 1 with p* >= 1 gives V = int u_s <= int |u_s| <= ||u_s||_{p*} ||1||_{(p*)'} = ||u_s||_{p*} V^{1 - 1/p*}, so ||u_s||_{p*} >= V^{1/p*}. The proof's other ingredients (||grad u_s||^2 = s^2 cap_D, trace = 1 - s, sum_j ||u_s||^2_{L^{p#}(B_j)} = (1 - s)^2 S, F_g(1) = c_N S/V^{2/p*}) then give F_g(u_s) <= F_g(1)[theta_D s^2 + (1 - s)^2]. At s* = 1/(1 + theta_D) this is theta_D/(1 + theta_D) F_g(1). The paper's step at l.885 (Minkowski, ||u_s|| >= V^{1/p*} - s||psi|| >= V^{1/p*}(1 - rho)) is valid but strictly weaker. The printed thm:upper is therefore true, since 0 < (1 - rho)^2 <= 1 for rho in [0, 1) and the bound is >= 0. The factor (1 - rho)^{-2} and the proviso rho < 1 are superfluous. The consequences claimed for eq:sandwich (right side theta_D/(1 + theta_D)) and for thm:sharp (l.212-215: eta -> 0 needs only theta_D/theta -> 1, so the rho -> 0 asserted at l.905 is unnecessary) follow. Toy check: toyPsi = (true -> -1, false -> 1) is the unique competitor of the two-point model (D = Bool -> R, boundary point false, counting measure), so it is the minimiser, |psi| = 1 everywhere, and rho = 1 exactly. Riemannian check (independent float integration): on the Euclidean unit ball in R^N the equilibrium potential is psi = 1 + (N+2)/2 (|x|^2 - 1) (Delta psi constant, mean 0), with psi(0) = -N/2. Its rho is 0.8736 (N = 3), 0.8801 (N = 4), 0.8926 (N = 5), 0.9041 (N = 6) and 0.9345 (N = 10).

findings.what: 'The proviso rho < 1 (l.878) does bite' rests on the two-point toy model only. There rho = 1 is exact and correct, but the toy model is not a Riemannian manifold. It shows that rho < 1 is not implied by the abstract model's axioms. It does not show that some (Sigma, g) of the paper's setting has rho >= 1. On the Euclidean 3-ball (a compact connected Riemannian 3-manifold with non-empty boundary) rho = 0.874 < 1 (lossy_check). The main finding, that the factor and the proviso are unnecessary, does not depend on this.
findings.fix: Reword for the author: 'on the abstract model the proviso is not automatic (toy_rho: rho = 1 on the two-point model); no (Sigma, g) with rho >= 1 is exhibited; the Jensen form needs no proviso in any case'.

findings.what: This is a library consistency point, not a defect of this file. The strict Capacity.lean counts InteriorBump (D contains a finite-energy interior function with int != 0, the paper's l.401 witness) among the reasons lem:capstar is partial. The strict rem:sign (cutoff chi) and now rem:notF1 (competitor psi) are marked while carrying the same kind of hypothesis, 'D contains a test function that the paper's setting guarantees'. The library applies two conventions to one kind of reading.
findings.fix: The master session should record one convention (a kb entry, or an OQ row for the author). This audit reads such existence hypotheses as part of the DEC-186 model of record when the setting guarantees them and a witness shows them satisfiable. Under that reading lem:capstar's partiality rests on MeanPoincare, TraceBound and DirectMethod alone. No change to Upper.lean.
